# Abstract

This gazetteer compiles settlement population series for the Southern Plains Hydrological Unit (HU 12) from 10000BC to 1600AD. Out of 93 ledger candidates evaluated in the regional ledger, 92 persistent mound centres, Balcones spring camps, High Plains hunter-gatherer sites and estuarine base settlements enter the active settlement inventory, while 1 duplicate coordinate alias within 2 km of George C. Davis is excluded. Catalogued settlements span from the Palaeoindian-Archaic Balcones spring complex at Gault (`65-210`) and High Plains sites at Lubbock Lake (`30-85`) and Blackwater Draw (`55-65`) through Caddoan centres George C. Davis (`1,65k` at 1200AD), Washington Square Mound (`950` at 1300AD), Pine Tree Mound (`640` at 1450AD), Hudnall-Pirtle (`480` at 1100AD) and Oak Hill Village (`460` at 1350AD) to protohistoric Waco-Wichita Village (`780` at 1600AD) and coastal base camps at Oso Creek-Corpus Christi (`460` at 1500AD) and Mitchell Ridge (`440` at 1500AD).

# Background

Unlike densely nucleated Mississippian alluvial corridors to the east, HU 12 exhibits a sharp contrast between fixed Caddoan mound towns in the Neches-Sabine pineywoods [@newell1949; @perttula2012] and seasonally mobile foraging or semi-sedentary prairie communities across the Edwards Plateau and Texas Gulf barrier bays [@perttula2004; @ricklis1996]. Kelly et al. [@kelly2025] radiocarbon summed probability curves (`N = 2.347`, peak 1287AD) reflect this dual structure, cresting during Middle Caddoan civic construction and late Holocene coastal intensification.

# Methodology

## Inclusion Criteria and Schema Audit

All 93 candidates in the regional source ledger were audited for exact WGS84 coordinates, multi-phase residential footprints and distinct spatial bounds. Included entries carry regional attribution linked directly to their hydrological sub-region and primary archaeological monographs documented in the supporting bibliography.

## Settlement Size Calibration

East Texas Caddoan populations at George C. Davis, Washington Square Mound, Pine Tree Mound, Oak Hill Village and Deshazo derive from excavated circular-post-structure zones and plaza-mound precincts [@newell1949; @perttula2012]. Central Texas spring camps, High Plains bison camps and coastal aggregates including Gault, Mitchell Ridge, Oso Creek-Corpus Christi and Waco-Wichita Village reflect multi-season base-camp midden extents and mortuary counts [@waters2011; @ricklis1994; @ricklis1996; @vehik2002].

# Testing and Validation

Ledger reconciliation and spatial containment checks across all 93 candidates returned `0` errors at GMT+0:

1. **Included Settlements**: 92 sites (`21` in Sabine-Neches Caddo, `63` in Brazos-Edwards and `8` in Gulf Coast-Nueces).
2. **Excluded Entries**: 1 duplicate coordinate and alias record within 2 km merged into George C. Davis.

# Results

## Top 45 Caddoan, Balcones and Coastal Settlements

Table \ref{tab:sp-included} presents the top 45 settlements by peak population descending out of the 92 catalogued sites in HU 12. Earliest documented occupations anchor along the Balcones spring line at Gault (`65` at 10000BC to `210` at 0AD) and Kincaid Shelter (`40` at 8600BC to `120` at 1400AD) alongside High Plains hunting sites at Lubbock Lake (`30` at 9800BC), Blackwater Draw Locality 1 (`55` at 9500BC), Aubrey (`35` at 9500BC), Siren (`25` at 9500BC) and Plainview (`35-45` around 8000BC) [@waters2011; @perttula2004].

In East Texas, George C. Davis grows from `450` in 800AD to `1,65k` in 1200AD before easing to `1,2k` in 1300AD [@newell1949; @perttula2012], complemented by Washington Square Mound (`520-950` across 1200-1400AD), Pine Tree Mound (`640` at 1450AD), Hudnall-Pirtle (`480` at 1100AD), Oak Hill Village (`460` at 1350AD), Deshazo (`380` at 1600AD), Gilbert (`320` at 1600AD), Lang Pasture (`310` at 1250AD) and Burr's Ferry Earthworks (`280` at 1200AD). Across the Brazos-Edwards prairies and Gulf barrier bays, Waco-Wichita Village reaches `780` by 1600AD [@vehik2002], while Harrell (`295` at 1400AD), Merchant (`265` at 1350AD), Mitchell Ridge (`440` at 1500AD), Oso Creek-Corpus Christi (`460` at 1500AD) and Cayo del Oso (`340` at 1450AD) sustain dense regional aggregations [@ricklis1994; @ricklis1996].

## Excluded Ledger Candidates

One candidate entry out of 93 in the regional source ledger is omitted from the active point gazetteer: a duplicate monument-inventory entry for George C. Davis falling within 2 km of the excavated Cherokee County precinct, merged into the primary George C. Davis record (`450` in 800AD to `1,65k` in 1200AD) to prevent spatial double-counting [@newell1949; @perttula2012].

# Limitations

Dispersed Caddoan farmstead hamlets across the Upper Neches, Angelina and Sulphur valleys outnumbered large mound centres in total population yet lack discrete nucleated town bounds, so they remain represented in sub-regional rural density rasters rather than individual gazetteer rows [@perttula2012]. The remaining 47 catalogued sites below rank 45 - primarily Balcones spring camps, burnt-rock midden stations and High Plains bison-kill localities peaking between `45` and `170` occupants - remain active in the spatial subtraction layer despite Table \ref{tab:sp-included} displaying only the leading 45 centres [@perttula2004].
